A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DiffusionNFT and provide readable text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A-D. Corresponding content can be matched reliably across pagination changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original SD3.5-Medium finetuning experiments, reward scores, training-efficiency comparisons, ablations, and generated-image examples.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds Table 2 with single-reward checkpoint evaluations for FlowGRPO and DiffusionNFT.

M1.justification: The positive/negative policy parameterization, training objective, reward normalization, EMA update, adaptive weighting, and Algorithm 1 are unchanged. Newly attributing adaptive weighting to DMD does not introduce a different procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same GenEval, OCR, Pick-a-Pic, and DrawBench coverage and reward tasks. Table 2 adds model configurations and results within this existing coverage.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparator methods remain FlowGRPO, the base-model/CFG configurations, SD-XL, SD3.5-L, and FLUX.1-Dev. Table 2 changes FlowGRPO's initialization setting rather than introducing another comparison method; DMD and CPS are cited but not evaluated.

E3.justification: Table 2 adds a comparison with both methods initialized from the CFG-free base model and reports checkpoints at different iteration counts. It also specifies enabling CFG for non-OCR evaluations of OCR-trained models. The existing experiments' protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 2 adds a common-initialization comparison and cross-reward evaluation of single-reward-trained models, examining generalization beyond their training reward and identifying an OCR-only generalization problem. The existing negative-loss, sampler, weighting, EMA, and guidance-strength ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for these results. The new discussion of gradient-estimation variance is theoretical, not empirical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 2 adds condition-specific results: FlowGRPO/DiffusionNFT attain GenEval scores of 0.97/0.98 at 4k/1k iterations and OCR scores of 0.96/0.97 at 1k/150 iterations, alongside cross-reward scores. Table 1 and the existing result figures are unchanged; the additions are not same-setting score corrections.

T1.justification: Appendix B.3 extends its existing FlowGRPO gradient analysis with Equations (23)-(26), using Stein's identity to connect it to reward backpropagation. This is a localized new derivation; the main DiffusionNFT theorems and Appendix A proofs are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal contributions retain the same forward-process, likelihood-free, solver-flexible reinforcement formulation and efficiency claims. The introduction and conclusion edits do not materially change their scientific scope.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly acknowledges impaired cross-reward generalization after OCR-only training. Appendix B.3 adds an interpretation of FlowGRPO as a higher-variance alternative to direct reward backpropagation that avoids differentiating through the remaining denoising trajectory.

D1.justification: For the added Table 2 comparison, v2 documents the common CFG-free initialization, checkpoint iteration counts, and the CFG exception when evaluating OCR-trained models. The existing Appendix C implementation recipe and project-access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to DMD by Yin et al. and Coefficients-Preserving Sampling by Wang and Yu. It also expands discussion of the already-cited DDO and connects FlowGRPO to ReFL, refining attribution and positioning without reorganizing the research context.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized introduction and explanatory edits, adds a cross-reference footnote and an LLM writing-assistance disclosure, and updates the publication header. The overall section structure and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 2 and redistributes existing material across pages, including Figure 5 and Figures 9-10. The original figures, qualitative image panels, and Table 1 retain their content and display design.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, Table 2 supplies a useful comparison from common CFG-free initialization and explicitly discloses the OCR generalization limitation and evaluation exception. The extended Appendix B.3 derivation and clearer attribution improve explanation. These are limited gains in transparency and analytical depth; the core method, benchmark coverage, and original efficiency evidence remain unchanged.
